idiom_name: DispatchQueue (serial/main) with async submission; AsyncStream for async sequences
implementation_notes: Dispatch provides the queue: DispatchQueue.main, the global concurrent queues and private serial queues accept blocks FIFO and run them on system-managed threads, async returns immediately so the sender is decoupled while asyncAfter defers work further, and a serial queue gives the single-consumer drain that marshals events to the main thread. What replaces the classic structure is submission - you do not build a queue, you submit to one - and an explicit array buffer is still justified when a render loop must coalesce events per frame or when an AsyncStream should not own the event lifetime.
pitfalls: DispatchQueue.main.sync deadlocks when called from the main queue, and any serial queue self-deadlocks the same way; use async for hand-off.
Blocks on a concurrent queue run in parallel: mutable state still needs its own synchronization, a serial queue or an actor.
Closures held by a queue extend captured object lifetimes - capture [weak self] or send value payloads instead of references.
